channel.title: CrimeTimeSnacks Blog
channel.description: True crime case updates, analysis, and the stories behind the headlines.

item.title: Why Some Cases Stay Cold for Decades
item.description: More than 345,000 U.S. homicides since 1965 are unsolved. Memory, evidence, tunnel vision and cost explain why some cases stall for decades.

item.title: Murders in Moscow: The Kohberger Plea and the Fight to Undo It
item.description: Bryan Kohberger pleaded guilty in 2025 to avoid a death sentence. In July 2026 he asked to withdraw that plea. Here is where the case stands.

item.title: How the FBI's ViCAP Database Links Violent Crimes
item.description: ViCAP, launched in 1985, lets police match violent crimes across jurisdictions. A 2024 federal audit found only 9 percent of agencies registered.

item.title: The Killing of JonBenét Ramsey: The Crime and the First Investigation
item.description: How six-year-old JonBenét Ramsey was found in her Boulder home in 1996, and what investigators did in the first ten years.

item.title: The First Fingerprint Convictions: Argentina, London, Chicago
item.description: A bloody thumbprint in Argentina in 1892, a cash box in London in 1905 and a painted railing in Chicago in 1910 brought fingerprints into court.

item.title: What Reasonable Doubt Actually Means in a Courtroom
item.description: The Constitution requires proof beyond a reasonable doubt but no set definition of it. Here is what the Supreme Court and jury instructions say.

item.title: How Wrongful Convictions Happen and How They Get Undone
item.description: What DNA exonerations and the National Registry of Exonerations show about eyewitness errors, false confessions and evidence that was withheld.

item.title: How Familial DNA Searching Works, and Where It Is Allowed
item.description: Familial searching looks for close relatives of an unknown offender in state DNA databases. How it works, cases it solved, and where it is legal.

item.title: How Cold Case Units Decide Which Files to Reopen
item.description: A cold case moves when a new lead exists: testable evidence, money for the lab, a database hit. The Sherri Rasmussen case shows how that works.

item.title: Why Eyewitness Testimony Is Less Reliable Than Jurors Think
item.description: Eyewitness misidentification played a role in 69 percent of 375 DNA exonerations. Here is what memory research says about why.

item.title: Chain of Custody: When Evidence Handling Sinks a Case
item.description: Chain of custody is the record of who handled evidence. Here is what the rules say about gaps, and when bad handling actually keeps evidence out.

item.title: How Forensic Genetic Genealogy Works, and the Rules Around It
item.description: How investigators turn crime scene DNA into a family tree, which databases they may search, and the rules written since the Golden State Killer arrest.

item.title: Why the JonBenét Ramsey Case Is Still Open After Nearly 30 Years
item.description: Unknown DNA, a grand jury vote that never became a charge, and what Boulder police say they are doing now in the JonBenét Ramsey case.

item.title: The Killing of Delaware Trooper Ty Snook at the Wilmington DMV
item.description: Cpl. Matthew "Ty" Snook was shot from behind at a Delaware DMV on Dec. 23, 2025. What the State Police found, and what has happened since.

item.title: The Watts Family Murders: The Weeks Before and the Evidence After
item.description: Chris Watts pleaded guilty in 2018 to killing his pregnant wife and two daughters. What the released case file shows about the weeks before and after.

item.title: Courtney Clenney: The Killing of Christian Obumseli and the Plea
item.description: Courtney Clenney pleaded guilty to manslaughter in the 2022 death of Christian Obumseli in Miami and was sentenced to six years. Here is the record.

item.title: How Investigators Tied Bryan Kohberger to the Moscow Murders
item.description: A car on camera, a phone that went quiet for two hours and DNA on a knife sheath: how investigators tied Bryan Kohberger to the Moscow killings.

item.title: The Menendez Brothers: Murders, Trials, Resentencing and Parole
item.description: How the 1989 Beverly Hills killings led to two trials, a 1996 life sentence, a 2025 resentencing, a parole denial and a March 2027 hearing.

item.title: The Delphi Murders: Bridge Guy, Richard Allen and the Appeal
item.description: Richard Allen was convicted in 2024 of killing Abby Williams and Libby German. The evidence, the trial, and where his appeal stands in October 2026.

item.title: Genetic Genealogy Cases: What It Has Solved and What It Cannot Do
item.description: From Angie Dodge to the Boy in the Box: cases genetic genealogy solved, the wrong turns along the way, and the limits courts and families still face.
